findings.statement: The five-minute assigned-camera capture did not satisfy the required cadence thresholds. The current eight-second functional smoke does not establish AC-4 cadence acceptance.
findings.expected: AC-4 requires at least 6,000 successfully published frames over five steady-state minutes, mean cadence of at least 20.0 fps, and no EOF-to-EOF interval above 60 ms, alongside matching cereal and VisionIPC frame IDs.
findings.observed: The earlier five-minute capture published 6,000 matching IDs but measured mean 19.999396661241942 fps, maximum EOF gap 123.185415 ms, and 743 of 5,999 intervals above 60 ms. The refreshed current-binding smoke lasted eight seconds and therefore is not cadence proof.
findings.remediation: health-check must produce an acceptance-passing five-minute capture on the assigned camera against the current package source hashes, preserving per-frame timestamps and dual-publication evidence. If the measured cadence still misses either threshold, return the concrete failure mechanism for a scoped build fix rather than treating the smoke as a pass.
findings.verification: Repeat the existing five-minute health-check capture procedure on the authorized assigned image node and inspect the per-frame EOF intervals. Pass only with at least 6,000 successfully published frames, mean cadence >=20.0 fps, every EOF gap <=60 ms, and matching IDs across cereal and VisionIPC; register the new probe inputs and log hashes in the package.

findings.statement: The package correctly retains the open SEC-FFMPEG-RESOURCE-001 residual: this host cannot enforce a safe per-child CPU/memory limit, so FFmpeg internal resource consumption remains unbounded. Dependency scanners remain not-run, not clean.
